identity.title: Adjust download interception strategy for the NDM extension

goal.goal: Adjust the NDM Chrome extension's download interception to support file-type filtering, without affecting other features (download management, status monitoring).
success_criteria: `ct.js` gains file-type filtering logic, and existing interception paths behave unchanged.
Manual test passes: MP4 files are intercepted, other types pass through normally.
`bg.js` requires no change (verify cross-context communication is unaffected).
constraints: Must keep the MV3 architecture using `chrome.storage.session` + `chrome.sendMessage`.
Do not change the existing download-management UI or interactions.

context.background: The NDM extension uses MV3. `ct.js` (content script) intercepts download links; `bg.js` (service worker) handles network monitoring and cross-context communication. The user wants tighter interception rules for specific file types, but worries about affecting existing features.

key_decisions.reason: interception happens at the content-script layer, so a local change is lower risk and matches "do not affect other features".
under MV3 the service worker may sleep; session storage is the most reliable cross-context option.

assumptions: The current `ct.js` concentrates interception in a single entry function (not yet confirmed line by line).

terminology.ct.js: content script that intercepts download links
terminology.bg.js: service worker that monitors network and handles cross-context communication

completed: Mapped the responsibilities and communication between `ct.js` and `bg.js`.
in_progress: Analyzing the interception function in `ct.js` line by line.
findings: `ct.js` does route every interception through a single entry function, so the assumption holds and no wrapper is needed.
The existing interception does not check file type at all, so adding a filter cannot break a prior type-based branch.

next_steps.action: Confirm the location and line numbers of the interception entry function in `ct.js`.
Design the insertion point for file-type filtering.
Implement the filtering logic with minimal changes.

risks: A filter-rule cache key-name collision with existing session data — avoid by using a dedicated namespace.

files.description: content script that intercepts download links; add filtering logic here.
service worker; not changed in this task.
extension manifest; sync if new permissions are added.

dependencies.name: Chrome (with the NDM extension)
dependencies.how_to_obtain: Install the latest stable Chrome and load the NDM extension for manual testing.

commands: Reload the extension in chrome://extensions to apply changes.

resume.how_to_resume: Open `F:\dev\ndm-extension\ct.js` and find the interception entry function (roughly in the second half of the file), then continue from the first `next_steps` item.
resume.contact: Task owner (reachable via the original conversation / workbench).
handoff_notes: The user prefers detailed technical explanations: architecture diagrams, line-by-line code breakdown, file paths with line numbers, and comparison tables.
For communication, `chrome.storage.session` is preferred over `chrome.sendMessage` (more reliable under MV3); new code should reuse the session approach.
